answer: Since the canyon escrow holds both sides, recruiting real counterparties is the operator's cost, and the garden audit releases each pair. A farm running 54 keys cannot self-supply these, because each counter-bonding peer must be independent on the lantern graph and each one exposes its own stake to the same slash. Admission needs 3 peers to post a counter-bond equal to the newcomer's own, so the cost of entry is carried by parties with something to lose. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
